children: The number of employed people in the United Kingdom rose by 67 thousand to 34.478 million in the three months in July 2026, following a gain of 83 thousand in the previous period.
The increase was the smallest since February, as a decline in part-time employment partly offset continued growth in full-time jobs.
Compared with a year earlier, employment rose by 243 thousand, driven by increases in both full-time employees and part-time self-employed workers.
The employment rate for people aged 16 to 64 stood at 75.1%, extending the broadly stable trend seen since mid-2024, while the rate for those aged 65 and over remained unchanged at 13.3%.
Meanwhile, the number of people holding second jobs increased over the quarter to 1.283 million, representing 3.7% of total employment.

title: UK Employment Posts Smallest Gain in 5 Months
